clue.text: Male nanny and market gardener

definitions.meaning: a man employed to look after children in a nursery
a person who raises plants and trees for sale

explanation.surface: A man who works as both a childminder and a grower of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a male nursery attendant and a professional plant grower who runs a nursery for seedlings.

clue.text: Wise old Greek provides home for fledgling soldiers

parts.note: a young bird lives in a nest
OR is short for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An elderly sage gives shelter to young recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fledgling soldiers' reads as one phrase about young recruits, but 'fledgling' belongs with 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer the aged king of Pylos is the archetype of sage counsel, so his name means a wise elder.

clue.text: Castle that is constructed by new recruit

parts.note: in chess the castle is also called a rook
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A fortress built by someone who has just joined up.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or raw beginner, especially a newly enlisted soldier, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: To show repentance, consume only modest fare

definitions.meaning: to apologise abjectly and admit one was wrong
read literally, to dine on a lowly pastry

explanation.surface: Doing penance by eating nothing but plain food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to admit an error humbly; read literally it is dining on a lowly pastry dish.

clue.text: Talks complainingly of small salary rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the pieces from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
pay is wages or salary

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a meagre pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns the whole of SPAY upwards in this down clue, giving YAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter or whine shrilly like a small dog is to talk on and on in a complaining way.

clue.text: A little hem needs repair constantly

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small hem that keeps coming down and has to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs repair' rearranges A LITTLE HEM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means continually or perpetually, without a break.

clue.text: Nothing should be added to -a blue dye

indicators.note: the word for nothing is placed after the letter a, joining them

parts.note: nil means nothing or zero

explanation.surface: An instruction that nothing more should go into a blue dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo obtained from a West Indian plant, a dark blue colouring agent.

clue.text: Lucky escape from a parsimonious young lady

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean
miss is the title of a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Fortunately avoiding a miserly girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape from disaster, something that almost happened.

clue.text: Taking home under a pound in one's apprenticeship

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece under another follows it

parts.note: L stands for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
earning is taking home pay

explanation.surface: Being paid less than a pound while training.
explanation.definitionFit: A period as an apprentice is a time of study and acquiring knowledge.

clue.text: Little time to produce a few charming words

definitions.meaning: a brief incantation, magic spoken briefly

explanation.surface: Briefly producing a short magic formula.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief period of time; read differently, a brief magic incantation.

clue.text: Convict returns to a celebration

indicators.note: a word that returns goes back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A released prisoner comes back for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convict' uses the slang 'old lag'; 'returns' is the reversal signal, not the convict coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion or special entertainment, a fete.

clue.text: Luxuriate when about to be embraced by resident boyfriend

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside another piece

parts.note: a live-in lover is a partner who lives with you
c, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: Enjoying luxury when your live-in partner hugs you.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to live in comfort and plenty, like cattle in a rich field.

clue.text: Repugnant swindle over promissory notes

indicators.note: over signals the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A distasteful scam involving written promises to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful or offensive, arousing disgust.

clue.text: President establishes many links around Sandhurst

indicators.note: the chain is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a chain is made of many links
Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA

explanation.surface: A president setting up connections with the British army officer college.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer training academy.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a meeting or company board.

clue.text: Graduate fed-up with a right-winger being vituperative

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A graduate sick of a Conservative politician becomes abusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed-up' looks like 'sick of', but 'up' reverses FED to DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive language damages reputations, so it is libellous or slanderous.

clue.text: Striking example of the stripper's aim?

definitions.meaning: an instructive demonstration of a principle
a stripper aims to end up wearing no items, a lesson without objects

explanation.surface: A vivid illustration of what an exotic dancer is trying to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical illustration teaching a point; whimsically, a performance that ends with no objects left.

clue.text: Leave one's pension by the supermarket counter

definitions.meaning: a pension is a boarding house, so to settle up and depart
the till where goods are paid for

explanation.surface: Someone cashing their pension at a supermarket till.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay and depart from a hotel or boarding house; also the till point in a shop.

clue.text: One in charge of a minor paper

definitions.text: One in charge of a minor
definitions.meaning: a person legally responsible for a child

explanation.surface: A person responsible for a child's newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal protector of a child; also the name of a British national daily newspaper.

clue.text: Central heating has a social function

definitions.meaning: a party to celebrate moving into a new home

explanation.surface: A radiator system that doubles as a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held when moving into a new home; read literally, heating the home.

clue.text: Ruth and Rex pursued by a heron

indicators.note: a piece pursued by another has that one following it

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king
an egret is a kind of heron

explanation.surface: Two people being chased by a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name, but ruth is an old word for sorrow or pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic noun for sorrow or remorse.

clue.text: Facade displayed by archdeacon perpetually

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A false front shown by a senior clergyman all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative surface layer, figuratively a superficial show.

clue.text: Prelate of sensual nature holds back primitive instincts

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it

parts.note: carnal means fleshly or sensual

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: in Freud the id is the seat of primitive instinct

explanation.surface: A churchman of fleshly temperament keeping his base urges in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ID into DI, which CARNAL holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior churchman of the Roman Catholic Church, a member of the Sacred College.

clue.text: Rip off a woollen coat

explanation.surface: Stealing someone's wool jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat someone out of money; also a sheep's wool covering.

clue.text: Rabbi least likely to harbour ill-humour

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, across the words

explanation.surface: The rabbi who is least inclined to bear a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bile was thought to cause bad temper, so it means irritability.

clue.text: Fail to award honour to Italian

indicators.note: one piece is attached to the next in sequence

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, an award

explanation.surface: Not giving a decoration to an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out or neglect to do something.

clue.text: Child's paper has five Irish limericks, perhaps

parts.note: a comic is a children's magazine
V is the Roman numeral five
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A children's magazine runs five Irish humorous poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Limericks are an example of humorous poetry.

clue.text: Flavour which can be put into a stock

definitions.text: which can be put into a stock
definitions.meaning: the projecting part of a blade fitted into a handle or stock

explanation.surface: A flavouring that can be added to soup stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong taste; also the shank of a tool fitted into its handle.

clue.text: Printer should be kind to author

parts.note: type means sort or kind
a writer is an author

explanation.surface: A printer ought to be nice to a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that prints letters onto paper.
